original_question: Let G be a bridgeless subcubic graph. If G is neither the Wagner graph nor the graph obtained from K_{3,3} by subdividing one edge, must chi_s(G) <= 9 hold?
target_in_paper: The nearest official formulation in arXiv:2210.05915 is Section 4.2, Conjecture 32(a), restated in Section 6 as item 10: if G is a subcubic graph that is bridgeless and is neither the Wagner graph nor the graph formed from the complete bipartite graph K_{3,3} by subdividing one edge, then χ_s(G) ≤ 9. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper very closely: it has the right graph class (bridgeless subcubic graphs), the two exact exceptional graphs, and the target bound 9. It is also correctly narrow: the paper does not add assumptions such as planarity, bipartiteness, girth, or connectivity to this statement. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))
missing_details: State explicitly that 'subcubic' means maximum degree at most 3 (equivalently, Δ(G) ≤ 3), since the paper’s statement begins 'Let G be a subcubic graph.' ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))

Define χ_s(G) explicitly as the strong edge-chromatic number (strong chromatic index): the minimum number of colors in an edge-coloring where any two edges at distance at most 2 receive distinct colors; equivalently, it is the chromatic number of the square of the line graph. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))

If you want the question fully stand-alone, unpack 'bridgeless' as 'having no bridge (cut-edge)'; the survey relies on standard graph-theory terminology rather than restating that definition. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))

For maximal fidelity, use the paper’s exact exception wording 'the graph formed from the complete bipartite graph K_{3,3} by subdividing one edge.' ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))
refined_question: Does every bridgeless graph G with maximum degree at most 3, other than the Wagner graph and the graph formed from the complete bipartite graph K_{3,3} by subdividing one edge, satisfy χ_s(G) ≤ 9, where χ_s(G) denotes the minimum number of colors in a strong edge-coloring of G, i.e. an edge-coloring in which any two edges at distance at most 2 receive distinct colors? ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, under the same hypotheses, is the square of the line graph of G 9-colorable? ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))
justification: Section 4.2 introduces the subcubic strong-edge-coloring program by recalling that every subcubic graph satisfies χ_s(G) ≤ 10 and then asking for structural conditions that force bounds 9, 8, 7, 6, or 5. Immediately after that setup, Conjecture 32(a) gives exactly the statement your draft is aiming at, and the survey later restates it verbatim as open problem 10 in Section 6. The nearby context also supplies the needed notation and definition of χ_s(G), so the only real issue with the draft is that those definitions are implicit rather than written out. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))
